releases.description: Yorushika's 1st full album and a concept album centered on n-buna's narrative. Features protagonist "Eimī", a young man who gives up music and travels through Sweden, writing letters to "Elma". 49m16s runtime, charted at #5 on Oricon with English title "Moonlight". Includes special limited edition wooden box packaging with letters and photos.

songs.notes: Theme song for the animated film

releases.description: Opening theme for the second cour of anime "Frieren: Beyond Journey's End." The song expresses the feeling of clearing weather and wishing for brightness, mirroring the characters' journey

songs.notes: Opening theme for anime; n-buna states the song is "about clearing, or more precisely wishing for clearing from a state of not clearing"

releases.description: 18th digital single by Yorushika. The title "Rubato" is a musical term referring to flexible tempo or elastic rhythm, allowing performers to naturally vary rhythm, speed, and musical timing to express emotion more freely. The song features introspective lyrics about seeking things that never become tiresome, with themes of memory, enjoyment, and sadness

songs.notes: Musical term meaning flexible/elastic tempo; explores themes of seeking lasting joy while reflecting on past musical attachments

releases.description: Written for the NTV drama "GO HOME Keishicho Mimotsumeinin Sodan-shitsu" about searching for missing persons. The song features piano and guitar with hand claps, expressing themes of disappearance and farewell. Influenced by poet Hakushū Kitahara's poetry

songs.notes: Theme song for NTV drama "GO HOME"; depicts a story of two living in a small house, with the protagonist wishing to be forgotten

releases.description: Ending theme for NHK anime "Chi: Earth's Motions." The philosophical title "Aporia" refers to an unsolvable problem or state of confusion. The song explores the desire to know unknowable things, with lyrics featuring a balloon as a metaphor for boundless knowledge

songs.notes: Ending theme for anime; mandolin recorded spontaneously the day after n-buna purchased the instrument

releases.description: Theme song for the Shochiku film "Shoutai," inspired by the motif of the sun with sunlight portrayed as butterfly wings. The song features collaboration with art director Tetsuga Nagato in their first project together since 2020. Themes include the sun illuminating all aspects of existence equally

songs.notes: Theme song for film; features art direction and music video by Tetsuga Nagato following collaboration on "Plagiarism" album; exhibition held in Harajuku

releases.description: Ending theme for NHK anime "Chi: Earth's Motions" (episodes 16+), replacing "Aporia." Inspired by Tang poet Yuan Zhen's poem "Parting Sorrow," the song explores awakening and knowledge with snake scales as a theme, featuring seasonal imagery from spring through winter

songs.notes: Ending theme for anime replacing "Aporia"; inspired by poet Yuan Zhen's classical Chinese verse; explores themes of awakening knowledge

releases.description: Opening theme for the second season of anime "Little Man Series." Inspired by poet Hagiwara Sakutaro's poem "Cat," the song explores the desire to escape to Mars as an ideal place. Features n-buna's directorial debut for the music video with piano-jazz instrumentation and artistic animation

songs.notes: Opening theme for anime; n-buna's directorial debut for music video; themes of escaping to Mars as idealistic alternative

releases.description: Theme song for Kansai TV/Fuji TV drama "We Don't Know the Rules of That Star Yet," inspired by Kenji Miyazawa's poetry collection "Spring and Asura." The neo-soul influenced song features drums, congas, and trumpet, exploring themes of internal struggle with a literary foundation

songs.notes: Theme song for drama; inspired by Kenji Miyazawa's "Spring and Asura"; features congas in Masack's debut and neo-soul style
